title: Design System: Badr Eddine ELBOUAMRI — Portfolio

display.purpose: H1–H3, section labels. IBM Plex Sans Condensed 600.

body.purpose: All prose and UI copy. IBM Plex Sans 400/500.

data.purpose: Every number, date, KPI, tool tag, figure caption, and Cartouche field — unconditionally.

shadows.name: card-hover-step
shadows.purpose: ProjectCard hover state — a flat drafting-ruler step, not ambient elevation. The system's only shadow.

motion.name: hero-reveal
motion.purpose: One orchestrated page-load reveal for hero content, staggered by ~80ms per element.

motion.name: cartouche-field-reveal
motion.purpose: Cartouche fields stamping in left-to-right/top-to-bottom on case-study load.

motion.name: nav-underline-sweep
motion.purpose: Nav link hover/focus underline — a ruler-tick sweep, not a fade.

motion.name: reduced-motion-override
motion.purpose: Disables all motion sitewide when requested.

components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Secondary Button

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: Header navigation link with ruler-tick underline sweep on hover/focus.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { position: relative; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; color: #14181b; text-decoration: none; padding-bottom: 2px; } .ds-nav-link::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: -2px; height: 1px; background: #0b5563; transform: scaleX(0); transform-origin: left; transition: transform 200ms ease-out; } .ds-nav-link:hover::after, .ds-nav-link:focus-visible::after { transform: scaleX(1); }

narrative.overview:
This is not a personal-brand site borrowing engineering motifs for flavor; it is styled as if the site itself were a piece of technical documentation — a drawing sheet, a routing card, a process standard. Every recurring device (the bordered field grid of the Cartouche, monospaced numeric data, hairline rules as the primary separator, small-caps mono eyebrows) is drawn from the actual vernacular of mechanical engineering paperwork, not from a generic 'clean minimal' aesthetic. Precision is the aesthetic: near-square corners, no shadows beyond a functional 1px hairline, no gradients, no decorative motion.

The palette reads as industrial instrumentation — petrol accent, graphite ink, amber for data emphasis only — deliberately avoiding both the generic 'engineering blue' of enterprise software and the warm cream/terracotta or near-black/acid palettes that now read as AI-generated template defaults. The typographic system is one superfamily (IBM Plex) used in three registers — condensed display for structure, regular sans for prose, mono for every number — which is what makes the numeric data (KPIs, dates, tool tags) visually legible as data rather than incidental text.
keyCharacteristics: Flat, bordered surfaces — hairline rules do the separating work cards-with-shadows would do elsewhere.
Near-square corners (2px max radius) everywhere; nothing rounds enough to feel soft.
Amber (--signal) is rationed to data emphasis only — KPI figures, chart highlights, active filters — never decoration.
All numeric content is monospaced, unconditionally, sitewide.
One signature structural device (the Cartouche) carries the site's entire visual personality; everything else stays quiet by comparison.
Motion is a single orchestrated on-load reveal per view — never scroll-jacking, never a hover transform beyond an instant color shift or a 2–3px nudge.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separation between regions is drawn with a 1px --rule border, never a box-shadow. The one sanctioned exception is the project card's hover state, which uses a flat 4px offset step-shadow, not ambient elevation.

rules.name: The Amber Rationing Rule
rules.body: If amber appears more than twice in a single viewport, remove one instance; it is a data-emphasis color, never a decorative one.

rules.name: The All-Numbers-Are-Mono Rule
rules.body: Every number on the site sets in --font-data, no exceptions. French number formatting applies in FR (comma decimal, non-breaking space before %).

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow softens or blurs. Where a shadow exists at all, it is a hard-edged flat offset used as a state cue, never as ambient depth.

rules.name: The One-Signature Rule
rules.body: The Cartouche's field-grid layout is exclusive to case studies. No other section may reuse its bordered-field-grid composition.

dos: Do set every number, date, and tag in --font-data (IBM Plex Mono) — no exceptions, sitewide.
Do use hairline (1px --rule) borders as the default separator between regions instead of shadows or card elevation.
Do keep border-radius at 2px or 0px — nothing rounder exists in this system.
Do ration --signal (amber) strictly to data emphasis: KPI figures, chart highlights, active filter state.
Do use structural numbering (01/02/03) only where the underlying content is genuinely sequential (DMAIC, 8D, process steps).
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, which zeroes out every animation/transition duration sitewide.
donts: Don't add gradients, glassmorphism, drop shadows beyond the one functional step-shadow, or particle/decorative effects.
Don't introduce a second bordered-field-grid layout outside the Cartouche.
Don't use amber, or any color, as pure decoration — every color in this system carries a semantic role.
Don't render skill/competency levels as percentage bars — use evidence links instead.
Don't introduce a second accent hue or a warmer/cooler neutral ramp without updating DESIGN.md first.
